categories.label: Data & Research
categories.blurb: Original empirical and data-driven research into antizionist rhetoric, belief, and media coverage.

categories.label: Essays & Commentary
categories.blurb: Analysis and opinion writing on antizionism as ideology and political culture.

categories.label: Substacks
categories.blurb: Independent newsletters covering antizionism, antisemitism, and Jewish identity.

resources.title: Essays on Antisemitism, Anti-Zionism, and the Left
resources.description: A posthumous English-language collection gathering Jean Améry's essays confronting antisemitism and antizionism, including his writings on the political currents of the postwar European left.
resources.reference: Améry, Jean. Essays on Antisemitism, Anti-Zionism, and the Left. Edited by Marlene Gallner. Translated by Lars Fischer. Indiana University Press, 2021.
resources.author: Jean Améry

resources.title: The Antizionist Complex
resources.description: One of the first book-length arguments that postwar hostility to Israel is a continuation of Judeophobia in a new guise; argues that opposition to Jewish national existence, however framed, ultimately derives from a refusal to accept a Jewish nation.
resources.reference: Givet, Jacques. The Antizionist Complex. SBS Publishing, 1979.
resources.author: Jacques Givet

resources.title: The History of Anti-Semitism
resources.description: A landmark four-volume history tracing Jew-hatred from antiquity through the rise of Nazism; the final volumes ("From Voltaire to Wagner," "Suicidal Europe") trace the emergence of racial antisemitism; Poliakov separately warned, in a 1969 book, that hatred of Jews might take on a new "anti-Zionist" guise.
resources.reference: Poliakov, Leon. The History of Anti-Semitism (multiple vols.). 1955–1977.
resources.author: Leon Poliakov

resources.title: The New Judeophobia
resources.description: Written in the wake of the 2001 Durban conference, argues that a "new Judeophobia," distinct from older racial antisemitism, diabolizes Israel and Zionism (and by extension Jews) using antiracist and anti-imperialist language rather than racial theory.
resources.reference: Taguieff, Pierre-André. The New Judeophobia. 2002.
resources.author: Pierre-André Taguieff

resources.title: Judeophobia: The Last Wave
resources.description: Continues Taguieff's study of the mutations of Judeophobia, extending his analysis of 'anti-Zionist antisemitism' into its most recent, post-2000s forms.
resources.reference: Taguieff, Pierre-André. Judeophobia: The Last Wave. 2018.
resources.author: Pierre-André Taguieff

resources.title: The Left against Zion: Communism, Israel, and the Middle East
resources.description: An edited volume examining the Soviet bloc's turn against Israel after 1967 and the antisemitic character much of that "anti-Zionist" campaign took on.
resources.reference: Wistrich, Robert S. (ed.). The Left against Zion. Vallentine, Mitchell, 1979.
resources.author: Robert S. Wistrich (ed.)

resources.title: From Ambivalence to Betrayal: The Left, the Jews, and Israel
resources.description: Traces the European left's shift from ambivalence toward, to eventual hostility against, Jews, Zionism, and Israel, from the origins of socialism in the 1840s to the present.
resources.reference: Wistrich, Robert S. From Ambivalence to Betrayal: The Left, the Jews, and Israel. University of Nebraska Press, 2012.
resources.author: Robert S. Wistrich

resources.title: A Lethal Obsession
resources.description: A sweeping single-volume history of antisemitism "from antiquity to the global jihad," ending with chapters connecting the Soviet war on Zionism and contemporary jihadist and left-wing antisemitism to older Judeophobic traditions.
resources.reference: Wistrich, Robert S. A Lethal Obsession. Random House, 2010.
resources.author: Robert S. Wistrich

resources.title: The Jews in the Soviet Union Since 1917: Paradox of Survival
resources.description: A detailed two-volume history of Soviet Jewry, including the state's campaigns against Zionism and Hebrew culture from the 1920s onward.
resources.reference: Levin, Nora. The Jews in the Soviet Union Since 1917: Paradox of Survival. NYU Press, 1988.
resources.author: Nora Levin

resources.title: Contemporary Left Antisemitism
resources.description: Analyzes how antisemitism that goes unacknowledged in left-wing and liberal spaces (unions, academia, campaigns to boycott Israel) can hide behind the language of anti-imperialism and human rights; develops Hirsh's concept of the "Livingstone Formulation," in which raising antisemitism is dismissed as a bad-faith attempt to silence criticism of Israel.
resources.reference: Hirsh, David. Contemporary Left Antisemitism. Routledge, 2017.
resources.author: David Hirsh

resources.title: From Antizionism to a New Middle East
resources.description: A collection of nine essays offering historical analysis, contemporary commentary, and practical solutions for a path to a multi-national and multi-religious Middle East, free of the mendacious and destructive force of antizionism.
resources.reference: Kirschbaum-Shirazki, Olga. From Antizionism to a New Middle East. 2026.
resources.author: Olga Kirschbaum-Shirazki

resources.title: Accusation in a Mirror
resources.description: Examines "accusation in a mirror," the propaganda technique documented before the Rwandan genocide of accusing one's intended victims of the very crimes one plans to commit, and traces it through Holocaust inversion and Iranian rhetoric that accuses Israel of genocidal intent while calling for its destruction. Argues that its use should satisfy the "directness" required to prosecute incitement to genocide.
resources.reference: Marcus, Kenneth L. "Accusation in a Mirror." Loyola University Chicago Law Journal, Vol. 43, No. 2, 2012.
resources.author: Kenneth L. Marcus

resources.title: Anti-Zionism & Anti-Semitism
resources.description: From the book examining how anti-Semitism should be defined; this chapter addresses where anti-Israel animus shades into anti-Semitism.
resources.reference: Marcus, Kenneth L. "Anti-Zionism & Anti-Semitism." In The Definition of Anti-Semitism, 146–190. Oxford University Press, 2015.
resources.author: Kenneth L. Marcus

resources.title: From Ambiguity to Accountability: The Case for a Legal Definition of Antisemitism in Academia
resources.description: Argues, using post–October 7 campus data, that universities should formally adopt the IHRA definition of antisemitism in their nondiscrimination policies to close the ambiguity around antizionism as a form of antisemitism and restore Title VI accountability.
resources.reference: Martin, Andrea J. "From Ambiguity to Accountability: The Case for a Legal Definition of Antisemitism in Academia." Pepperdine Law Review, 2025.
resources.author: Andrea J. Martin

resources.title: Hamas' October 7th Genocide: Legal Analysis and the Weaponisation of Reverse Accusations
resources.description: Argues under the Genocide Convention that Hamas's October 7 attack itself meets the legal definition of genocide, and examines how the reverse "genocide" accusation against Israel functions to deflect that recognition.
resources.reference: Shalev, Avraham Russell. "Hamas' October 7th Genocide: Legal Analysis and the Weaponisation of Reverse Accusations—A Study in Modern Genocide Recognition and Denial." Israel Law Review, Vol. 58, Special Issue 2–3, 2025.
resources.author: Avraham Russell Shalev

resources.title: The Genocide Libel: How the World Has Charged Israel with Genocide
resources.description: Traces how genocide accusations against Israel, unlike those leveled at other states, have persisted throughout its existence, and argues the post-October 7 version deploys classic antisemitic tropes (blood libel, Nazi inversion, collective Jewish guilt).
resources.reference: Goda, Norman J. W. "The Genocide Libel: How the World Has Charged Israel with Genocide." ISCA Research Paper 2025-3, Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism, Indiana University, 2025.
resources.author: Norman J. W. Goda

resources.title: On Three Antizionisms
resources.description: Argues that "antizionism" is not one coherent ideology but three distinct ideological clusters that happen to share a label, and that treating them as one obscures more than it clarifies.
resources.reference: Mor, Shany. "On Three Antizionisms." Israel Studies, Vol. 24, No. 2, 2019.
resources.author: Shany Mor

resources.title: Demonization Blueprints: Soviet Conspiracist Antizionism in Contemporary Left-Wing Discourse
resources.description: Traces how Soviet-era "anti-Zionist" propaganda campaigns (1967–88) built a conspiracist, demonizing template for talking about Israel that Tabarovsky argues has been absorbed largely intact into today's left-wing discourse.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. "Demonization Blueprints: Soviet Conspiracist Antizionism in Contemporary Left-Wing Discourse." Journal of Contemporary Antisemitism, vol. 5, no. 1, 2022, pp. 1-20.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: The Anti-Zionist Mythology of the Left
resources.description: A shorter companion piece to Wistrich's From Ambivalence to Betrayal, dissecting the intellectual myths (Zionism as racism, colonialism, imperialism) that underpin the contemporary left's hostility to Israel.
resources.reference: Wistrich, Robert S. "The Anti-Zionist Mythology of the Left." Israel Journal of Foreign Affairs, 9:2, 2015.
resources.author: Robert S. Wistrich

resources.title: American Antizionism
resources.description: Argues that post-October 7 antizionism in the U.S. is best understood not as an intellectual critique of Zionism but as a mass political and social movement, with roots traced back through Poliakov's own 1969 prediction of a coming "anti-Zionist" mutation of antisemitism.
resources.reference: Kelner, Shaul. "American Antizionism." Sources: A Journal of Jewish Ideas, Fall/Winter 2025.
resources.author: Shaul Kelner

resources.title: "Anti-Zionism" and "Antizionism"
resources.description: Subtitled "the anti-Jewish worldview behind anti-Israel obsessions," it argues antizionism functions as a self-contained worldview that constructs its own caricature of Israel and positions it as central to global oppression.
resources.reference: Hirsh, David. "'Anti-Zionism' and 'Antizionism'." Australia/Israel & Jewish Affairs Council.
resources.author: David Hirsh

resources.title: Defeating Antizionism
resources.description: Argues antizionism should be named and fought as its own distinct hate ideology rather than folded into debates over "antisemitism."
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. "Defeating Antizionism." Sapir, Issue 12, 2026.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: What Antizionism Really Is
resources.description: Continues Louis-Klein's argument that antizionism is a structured ideology with its own libels (colonizer, apartheid, genocide) rather than simply a political stance on Israeli policy.
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. "What Antizionism Really Is." The Free Press.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: Rwanda, Israel and the Inversion of 'Genocide'
resources.description: Argues that today's genocide accusations against Israel by defenders of Hamas follow the same rhetorical playbook Hutu extremists used against Tutsis in Rwanda in the early 1990s — inverting the language of genocide to accuse the actual targets of it.
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. "Rwanda, Israel and the Inversion of 'Genocide.'" The Wall Street Journal, July 22, 2026.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: The Left-Wing Case Against Anti-Zionism
resources.description: Makes the case, aimed at a left-leaning audience, that opposing antizionism is consistent with — not opposed to — progressive values.
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. "The Left-Wing Case Against Anti-Zionism." The Atlantic.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: The Cult of Antizionism
resources.description: Examines the founding of an academic "Institute for the Critical Study of Zionism" as an attempt to revive the Soviet-era discipline of "scientific antizionism" within American universities.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. "The Cult of 'Antizionism.'" Tablet Magazine.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Zombie Antizionism
resources.description: Discussion of how Soviet-origin antizionist tropes, long assumed dead, keep resurfacing largely unchanged in Western left-wing discourse.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. "Zombie Antizionism." Tablet Magazine.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Soviet Antizionism and Contemporary Left Antisemitism
resources.description: Lays out how the USSR's Cold War-era antizionist propaganda apparatus supplied the conspiratorial vocabulary and imagery still used against Israel and Zionism today.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. "Soviet Antizionism and Contemporary Left Antisemitism." Fathom Journal.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Antizionism: Projection and Replacement Theology
resources.description: Argues that antizionism in its Soviet, progressive, Islamist, Nazi, Christian, and Enlightenment-liberal forms shares two structures: a projection onto Israel of whatever each group considers evil, and a "replacement theology" in which one culture or ideology claims to supersede Judaism and so sees no need to understand Jews on their own terms. Calls for exposing replacement theology in education alongside antizionist libels.
resources.reference: Kirschbaum-Shirazki, Olga. "Antizionism: Projection and Replacement Theology."
resources.author: Olga Kirschbaum-Shirazki

resources.title: They Don't Believe It Either
resources.description: Argues that much of the post-October 7 "genocide" rhetoric aimed at Israel functions less as a sincerely held factual belief than as a performative, tribal signal.
resources.reference: Boudry, Maarten. "They Don't Believe It Either." Quillette, Oct. 19, 2025.
resources.author: Maarten Boudry

resources.title: The Shadow of Babi Yar: How the Soviets Taught the West to Erase the Jews
resources.description: Uses the Soviet-era suppression of the memory of the Babi Yar massacre as a case study for how erasing Jewish victimhood became a template later adopted by Western antizionist discourse.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. "The Shadow of Babi Yar: How the Soviets Taught the West to Erase the Jews." Jewish Journal.
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: Three Failed Strategies of Inward Advocacy
resources.description: Argues that Jewish communal advocacy has relied on three failed strategies of "inward advocacy" (self-promotion, aligning Israel with fashionable values, and correcting facts) that treat antizionist libels as misinformation and keep Jews in the defendant's seat. Calls for turning the lens on the accuser by exposing antizionism's Soviet origins and teaching ideological literacy.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. "Three Failed Strategies of Inward Advocacy." JNS.
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: Scaffolding Anti-Zionism: The Hate We Missed
resources.description: Argues that teaching antisemitism as generic intolerance and scapegoating has left people unable to recognize antizionism as the third, mutated form of Jew-hatred after anti-Judaism and antisemitism, one that constructs Jews as villains through libels such as "Zionism is racism." Calls for education that exposes antizionist libels as earlier generations exposed antisemitic ones.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. "Scaffolding Anti-Zionism: The Hate We Missed." Jewish Journal, 2025.
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: The Eternal Settler
resources.description: Written after a wave of antisemitic attacks in Montreal, argues that even long-established Diaspora communities such as Canada's (not just Israelis) are increasingly branded "settlers" in antizionist rhetoric — a designation Wexler argues has no logical stopping point.
resources.reference: Wexler, Benjamin. "The Eternal Settler." K. (Les Juifs, l'Europe, le XXIe siècle), June 20, 2024.
resources.author: Benjamin Wexler

resources.title: The History of the Charge of Genocide Against Israel
resources.description: A two-part historical investigation tracing the "genocide" accusation against Israel back through the revival of Arab nationalism (1920s–40s) and its absorption of European fascist and antisemitic ideas, then showing how those ideological roots fed the settler-colonialism framework used to level the charge today.
resources.reference: Szeftel, Daniel. "The History of the Charge of Genocide Against Israel." K. (Part 1 and Part 2).
resources.author: Daniel Szeftel

resources.title: The Greatest Threat to Jewish Safety Has a New Name
resources.description: Argues that antizionism, rather than traditional far-right antisemitism, has become the primary vector of anti-Jewish hostility today.
resources.reference: Dabelstein, Joshua. "The Greatest Threat to Jewish Safety Has a New Name." Australian Financial Review.
resources.author: Joshua Dabelstein

resources.title: A Deep Historical Irony of Anti-Zionism: Lessons from Poland
resources.description: Draws on Poland's 1968 state-orchestrated "anti-Zionist" purge, in which the label "Zionist" functioned as a euphemism for "Jew" and drove out most of the country's remaining Jewish population all while antisemitism was illegal.
resources.reference: McCallum, Alasdair. "A Deep Historical Irony of Anti-Zionism: Lessons from Poland." The Jewish Independent.
resources.author: Alasdair McCallum

resources.title: I've Seen This Before
resources.description: Interactive data analysis on the overlap of Soviet anti-Zionist propaganda and today's antizionist speech.
resources.reference: "I've Seen This Before." Data analysis, mapping Soviet anti-Zionist propaganda to modern echoes using semantic similarity.

resources.title: Antizionism Is a Totalitarian Conspiracy Theory Rotting the West From Within
resources.description: Argues antizionism is not ordinary criticism of Israeli policy but a modernized, eliminationist hate ideology with its own closed analytical framework, comparable to other totalizing conspiracy theories.
resources.reference: Heath, Allister. "Antizionism Is a Totalitarian Conspiracy Theory Rotting the West From Within." The Telegraph.
resources.author: Allister Heath

resources.title: Antizionism Is Not Antisemitism
resources.description: Argues that treating antizionism as one species of "antisemitism" undersells it as its own freestanding ideology of Jew-hatred.
resources.reference: Kaufman, Rona. "Antizionism Is Not Antisemitism." The Times of Israel Blogs.
resources.author: Rona Kaufman

resources.title: The Court Is Wrong: Antizionism Is Discriminatory
resources.description: Argues that a specific court ruling wrongly treated antizionist conduct as protected political speech rather than as discriminatory conduct against Jewish people.
resources.reference: Kaufman, Rona. "The Court Is Wrong: Antizionism Is Discriminatory." The Times of Israel Blogs.
resources.author: Rona Kaufman

resources.title: The Antizionist Movement Is a Hate Movement: It's Time to Say So
resources.description: Written after the 2025 Bondi Beach Hanukkah attack in Australia, argues — using the Southern Poverty Law Center's own definition of an antisemitic hate group — that the antizionist movement now meets that standard.
resources.reference: Martin, Andrea J. "The Antizionist Movement Is a Hate Movement: It's Time to Say So." The Times of Israel Blogs.
resources.author: Andrea J. Martin

resources.title: When Courts Minimize Terrorism, Jewish Students Pay the Price
resources.description: Argues that a federal appeals court's minimizing description of the October 7 terror attack, in a ruling on Jewish students' claims against MIT, leaves Jewish students unprotected under civil-rights law.
resources.reference: Martin, Andrea J. "When Courts Minimize Terrorism, Jewish Students Pay the Price." The Times of Israel Blogs.
resources.author: Andrea J. Martin

resources.title: The BDS Pound of Flesh
resources.description: Argues that BDS-style campaigns to publicly shame students into disavowing Israel are a deliberate strategy to raise the "psychic and professional cost" of being Jewish.
resources.reference: Wilf, Einat. "The BDS Pound of Flesh." Tablet Magazine.
resources.author: Einat Wilf

resources.title: Moral Inversion and the Rise of Authoritarian Sympathy
resources.description: A data study finding that antizionist views correlate with a broader "moral inversion" — a systematic tendency to misjudge or invert the actual human-rights records of authoritarian versus democratic states.
resources.reference: Dulberg, Zack, et al. Moral Inversion and the Rise of Authoritarian Sympathy. Rutgers University Social Perception Lab / Network Contagion Research Institute.
resources.author: Zack Dulberg et al.

resources.title: Anti-Judaism: The Western Tradition
resources.description: Argues that anti-Judaism is not a fringe extremism but a foundational conceptual tool of Western thought itself. Nirenberg shows that Jews have represented what societies tend to define themselves against. Traces this paradigm from antiquity through the Enlightenment and just past the Holocaust.
resources.reference: Nirenberg, David. Anti-Judaism: The Western Tradition. W.W. Norton & Co., 2013.
resources.author: David Nirenberg

resources.title: The Final Solution to the Jewish Question: A Love Story for the Living
resources.description: A follow-up to Horn's People Love Dead Jews, drawing on her post-October 7 work with university presidents and the U.S. government; diagnoses failures of Holocaust education and the long history of antizionism, and proposes a path forward.
resources.reference: Horn, Dara. The Final Solution to the Jewish Question: A Love Story for the Living. Simon & Schuster, 2026.
resources.author: Dara Horn

resources.title: Be a Refusenik: A Jewish Student's Survival Guide
resources.description: Pairs the stories of Soviet-era refuseniks — Jews who defied a state doctrine equating Zionism with racism and genocide — with those of Jewish students facing similar antizionist pressure on American campuses today, drawing practical strategies from the earlier movement. Foreword by Natan Sharansky.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. Be a Refusenik: A Jewish Student's Survival Guide. Wicked Son, 2025.
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Movement Against Antizionism
resources.description: A non-partisan, emergency-response initiative confronting a rapidly escalating antizionist hate movement that is actively endangering Jewish communities worldwide.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism. Movement Against Antizionism (Substack).
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism

resources.title: Movement Against Antizionism AU
resources.description: Australian affiliate of the Movement Against Antizionism, led by Joshua Dabelstein; grassroots training and education on antizionism.
resources.reference: Movement Against Antizionism Australia. Movement Against Antizionism AU (Substack).
resources.author: Movement Against Antizionism Australia

resources.title: Institute for the Critical Study of Antizionism
resources.description: To promote the critical study of the most current manifestation of the world's oldest hatred.
resources.reference: Pessin, Andrew. Institute for the Critical Study of Antizionism (Substack).
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: Jennifer Kogan
resources.description: "Jewish Fierce Compassion": a clinical social worker analyzes antizionism through a psychological-abuse framework. Levari, offering trauma-informed education on antizionism, publishes here too.
resources.reference: Kogan, Jennifer. Jennifer Kogan (Substack).
resources.author: Jennifer Kogan

resources.title: Adam Louis-Klein
resources.description: Newsletter by the anthropologist and founder of the Movement Against Antizionism (MAAZ).
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. Adam Louis-Klein (Substack).
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: Naya's Newsletter
resources.description: Politics, education, history, antisemitism, and Jewish identity.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. Naya's Newsletter (Substack).
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: Pariah--But The Truth, You Know, Ain't A Democracy
resources.description: Musings both non-fictional and fictional (it can sometimes be hard to tell the difference).
resources.reference: Pessin, Andrew. Pariah (Substack).
resources.author: Andrew Pessin

resources.title: The New Refuseniks
resources.description: Exploring themes from Tabarovsky's research and writing on Soviet and contemporary antizionism, Jewish identity, freedom, courage, and resistance.
resources.reference: Tabarovsky, Izabella. The New Refuseniks (Substack).
resources.author: Izabella Tabarovsky

resources.title: Einat Wilf
resources.description: Speaker and writer.
resources.reference: Wilf, Einat. Einat Wilf (Substack).
resources.author: Einat Wilf

resources.title: Beyond Belief
resources.description: Israel, the Middle East, and the politics, philosophy, and history that still burn beneath them.
resources.reference: Hyde, Samuel J. Beyond Belief (Substack).
resources.author: Samuel J. Hyde

resources.title: After October 7
resources.description: Original watchdog reporting on Jewish issues, helping readers make sense of the post-October 7 world.
resources.reference: Deutsch, Kevin. After October 7 (Substack).
resources.author: Kevin Deutsch

resources.title: COUNTERINTUITIVE
resources.description: Commentary by writer David Christopher Kaufman on antizionism, Jewish identity, and politics.
resources.reference: Kaufman, David Christopher. COUNTERINTUITIVE (Substack).
resources.author: David Christopher Kaufman

resources.title: For Normal People
resources.description: Reader-funded publication by Australian writer Joshua Dabelstein, combining political and cultural analysis, reviews, and philosophical meanderings.
resources.reference: Dabelstein, Joshua. For Normal People (Substack).
resources.author: Joshua Dabelstein

resources.title: Being Jewish with Jonah Platt
resources.description: Interviews on Jewish identity and antizionism from a mainstream, entertainment-adjacent angle.
resources.reference: Platt, Jonah. Being Jewish with Jonah Platt (Substack).
resources.author: Jonah Platt

resources.title: Sarah Ettedgui
resources.description: A Mizrahi/Sephardic lawyer writing on antizionism in society.
resources.reference: Ettedgui, Sarah. Sarah Ettedgui (Substack).
resources.author: Sarah Ettedgui

resources.title: Antizionism as a Distinct Anti-Jewish Bigotry
resources.description: Argues antizionism is a coherent ideology with its own genealogy (Nazi-Islamist axis, Soviet propaganda, Western settler-colonial theory) and a recurring triad of libels (colonizer, apartheid, genocide) — and that it inverts classical antisemitism: where the old hatred cast Jews as alien outsiders, antizionism denies Jewish peoplehood and indigeneity outright.
resources.reference: Louis-Klein, Adam. 'Antizionism as a Distinct Anti-Jewish Bigotry.' Journal of Contemporary Antisemitism, Vol. 9, No. 1, 2026.
resources.author: Adam Louis-Klein

resources.title: The Polish Exodus of 1968: Antisemitism, Dropouts, and Re-emigrants in Nowiny i Kurier
resources.description: Examines how Nowiny i Kurier, Israel's Polish-language newspaper, covered the 1968 anti-Zionist and antisemitic campaign in Poland that drove out nearly 13,000 Jews, including the emigrants who settled outside Israel and those who later moved again.
resources.reference: Freilich, Miri, and Sharon Levinas. "The Polish Exodus of 1968: Antisemitism, Dropouts, and Re-emigrants in Nowiny i Kurier." Polin: Studies in Polish Jewry, Vol. 35, 2023, pp. 337–352.
resources.author: Miri Freilich and Sharon Levinas

resources.title: The Soviet "Doctors' Plot"—50 Years On
resources.description: Revisits Stalin's 1953 accusation that a group of mostly Jewish doctors had plotted against the Soviet leadership, the only one of his show trials that never took place because he died first. Argues the affair reveals Stalin's politics and the survival of overt antisemitism in the postwar Soviet Union.
resources.reference: Clarfield, A. Mark. "The Soviet 'Doctors' Plot'—50 Years On." BMJ, Vol. 325, No. 7378, 2002, pp. 1487–1489.
resources.author: A. Mark Clarfield

resources.title: On Antizionism and Unlearning Arab Supremacy
resources.description: Argues that much contemporary antizionism rests on unexamined assumptions of Arab political and cultural primacy in the Middle East, denying Jewish indigeneity and minimizing the historic persecution and displacement of Middle Eastern Jews. Calls for 'unlearning Arab supremacy' the same way other forms of ethnic or colonial privilege get critically examined.
resources.reference: Bacharach, Barak. 'On Antizionism and Unlearning Arab Supremacy.' Haverford College Political Science Department, Alumni Corner.
resources.author: Barak Bacharach

resources.title: March '68. Historical Facts
resources.description: The POLIN Museum's own historical account of the March 1968 crisis: a suppressed student rally that the Polish communist authorities turned into a state-run antisemitic campaign, forcing roughly 13,000 Polish Jews out of the country and effectively ending organized Jewish life in Poland.
resources.reference: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews. 'March '68. Historical Facts.'
resources.author: POLIN Museum of the History of Polish Jews

resources.title: 13,000 Jews Were Driven Out of Poland in 1968. Now, Some Are Returning to Tell Their Story.
resources.description: Follows Polish-Jewish emigrants of the 1968 antisemitic purge who returned to Poland decades later on an Engaged Memory Consortium trip, revisiting the state-run 'anti-Zionist' campaign that stripped them of jobs, schools, and citizenship, and reckoning with how little-known this history remains today.
resources.reference: Bartov, Shira Li. '13,000 Jews Were Driven Out of Poland in 1968. Now, Some Are Returning to Tell Their Story.' SA Jewish Report (via JTA), June 15, 2026.
resources.author: Shira Li Bartov

resources.title: The 1968 Forced Exodus of Polish Jewry on Film
resources.description: Surveys how Polish filmmakers have documented and interpreted the 1968 'March emigration' on screen, from Marian Marzyński's own exile documentary Skibet/Hatikvah through later films grappling with Polish-Jewish identity and the anti-Zionist purge that provoked it.
resources.reference: Shpolberg, Masha. 'The 1968 Forced Exodus of Polish Jewry on Film.' Tablet Magazine, May 1, 2018.
resources.author: Masha Shpolberg

resources.title: Center of Attention: Why One of the World's Tiniest Countries Gets the Biggest International Spotlight
resources.description: Argues Israel receives 7 to 600 times more international news coverage per capita than countries such as Canada, Brazil, and India, regardless of active conflict, and traces that disparity to a deliberate, decades-long influence campaign rooted in Soviet-era intelligence operations and sustained by later institutional and funding networks; draws on the author's GDELT-based media-coverage dataset (see companion methodology piece).
resources.reference: Musighi, Jeremy. "Center of Attention: Why One of the World's Tiniest Countries Gets the Biggest International Spotlight." profoundAF, Aug. 27, 2026.
resources.author: Jeremy Musighi

resources.title: Where the Soviets Won
resources.description: Argues that Soviet state antizionism collapsed with the USSR because the Soviet intelligentsia recognized it as official propaganda, while in the West the same educated class embraced it voluntarily after it arrived in the 1960s–70s attached to the language of antiracism. Calls for reforming American education so that antisemitism is no longer taught only as a form of racial hatred.
resources.reference: Lekht, Naya. "Where the Soviets Won." Sapir, Volume 22, Summer 2026.
resources.author: Naya Lekht

resources.title: The Forever Genocide
resources.description: Argues that the genocide accusation against Israel predates October 7, tracing it from Soviet and Arab propaganda after 1967 to NGOs and academia, and contends it functions as a predetermined moral label rather than a legal finding. resources.title: Genocide for Dummies
resources.description: Argues that Gaza does not meet the legal threshold of genocide, setting out the Genocide Convention's special-intent requirement and the 'only reasonable inference' standard, comparing the recognized cases (Holocaust, Rwanda, Srebrenica, Cambodia, Darfur), and contending that the war's death toll, demographics and conduct point to a war against Hamas rather than an intent to destroy Palestinians as such. resources.title: Soviets taught the West to hate Israel.

resources.title: Obama's revisionist 'Promised Land'

resources.title: The radical Left's merger with Islamist despotism

resources.title: How Objectionable is the Conn College Faculty-Staff "Statement of Solidarity"?

resources.title: The Palestine Propaganda Complex
resources.description: Argues that words like 'Palestine,' 'refugee,' 'apartheid' and 'genocide' have been emptied of their original meanings and recycled through academia and the UN in a 'placard strategy' that equates Zionism with evil, updating older blood libels. resources.title: The History They Hope You Never Learn About 'From the River to the Sea'

resources.title: A Letter to Golda
resources.description: Recounts the 1969 'Letter of the Eighteen,' in which Georgian Jewish families openly petitioned Israel and the UN for permission to emigrate, and traces how it galvanized Soviet Zionists, Israeli policy and the later exodus of 1.5 million Soviet Jews. Draws on interviews with surviving participants and reflects on what the story means for American Jews.

resources.title: Meet the Architects of Academic Antizionism (Dispatch #13)
resources.description: Traces a roughly century-long genealogy of antizionism in academia, from Soviet and Arab nationalist propaganda through postcolonial theory and settler-colonial theory to the construction of the genocide libel. resources.title: Antizionism Is Not Jewish Anti-Zionism (Dispatch #12)
resources.description: Argues that conflating pre-1948 Jewish anti-Zionism, a set of intra-Jewish debates, with contemporary antizionism, which he characterizes as a hate ideology denying Jews the right to political self-determination, gives the latter cover and endangers Jewish communities. Urges hyphenation-based terminological precision, naming antizionism as hate, and asking non-Jews for help in interrupting it.
